requirements.statement: `spindlebox index` writes a top-level `types` list to .spi/index.json. Every entry has `name`, `kind` (record or variant) and `type_params` (a list of names); a record has `fields` [{name, type}] in declaration order, a variant has `variants` [{name, fields}] in declaration order, with `fields` empty for a payload-free variant.

parameters.canonical: canonical form: record <Name>[<T,..>]{<field>:<type>,..} | variant <Name>[<T,..>]{<Variant>[{<field>:<type>,..}],..}; type references are obj:<Name>[<args>], type parameters typevar:<Name>, other types core-1 (str, i64, f64, list<>, map<,>, option<>)

requirements.statement: The five indexes give identical canonical forms for the seven model types, except TypeScript's f64 where the others have i64 (DS-TS). One model is one normalized shape whichever language declared it.
In every index, each obj:<Name> inside a model type's canonical form names a type in that index's `types`, and no model type contains `any`: nothing is erased.
In every index the function `total` has exactly one non-receiver parameter of norm_type obj:Order and returns obj:Money.

For each of the five model indexes, `spindlebox generate --lang java` writes Java that declares the seven model types; javac compiles it; and indexing the generated Java gives back the source index's canonical forms for the seven model types (TypeScript's f64 stays f64).

requirements.statement: For each of the five model indexes, `spindlebox generate --lang rust` writes Rust that declares the seven model types; indexing the generated Rust gives back the source index's canonical forms; and where cargo is installed, `cargo check --offline` on the generated crate passes. Where cargo is absent the compile check is reported as skipped, never as passed (#27).

In the generated Java, `total` is declared as `<..Money> total(<..Order> <name>)`; in the generated Rust, as `fn total(<name>: [&]<..Order>) -> <..Money>`; neither uses an opaque stand-in (Object, serde_json::Value) for those types.
